title: Large Language Models Naively Recover Ethnicity from Individual Records
benchmark_measurement: The accuracy of inferring religious sect from names in a Lebanese dataset and inferring religious group distributions from names in an Indian dataset.
findings: Large Language Models can infer religious sect from Lebanese names with up to 64.3% accuracy, performing best on groups with distinctive naming conventions like Armenian Orthodox (97.4%) and Shia (90.4%). For aggregate validation in India, the models' inferred Hindu and Muslim population shares were within 0.5 percentage points of census data, demonstrating an ability to recover known religious distributions from names.
